paras: The lynching of Spence was the hanging of a young Black man near Frog Level, Caddo Parish, Louisiana, in mid-July 1881. Spence, said to be about 18, was accused of trying to enter a girl's room at a local house and was later found hanged. A Shreveport paper approved the killing under the heading 'Quick Justice', and the item was reprinted in Louisiana and Tennessee.

According to a Shreveport account based on 'a gentleman living in the neighborhood', Spence had twice attempted to enter the room of an orphan girl who lived with Mr. J. E. Spearman. On one of those occasions he had been tied up but got away.

A few nights before the report, Spence was said to have tried again to enter the room, which by then was occupied by two visiting women while the girl slept elsewhere. That attempt 'resulted in his capture', and he was afterward 'found hung in the neighborhood of Frog Level'. None of the accounts names his captors, says how many took part, or gives the place or time of the hanging.
No report of an inquest, arrest or official response appears in the coverage.

The Richland Beacon of Rayville printed the account on July 23 under the heading 'QUICK JUSTICE', credited to the Shreveport Standard, which called the alleged act a 'damnable design' and said Spence 'was dealt with as he should have been'. A week later the Donaldsonville Chief ran nearly the same text among its state news, crediting the Shreveport Telegram and giving the householder's initials as 'J. B.'. Neither Louisiana text used the word lynching; both described Spence as 'found hung'.

The Milan Exchange in Tennessee reduced the story on July 30 to a single line in its Louisiana column, stating that Spence was lynched near 'Frog Levee', Caddo Parish, 'last week for an attempt at rape'. That brief was the only report to call the killing a lynching or to name the accusation as attempted rape, and it carried no comment. All three reports appear to rest on the same Shreveport item, and no other account of the killing was found.

reader.title: Lynching of Spence
bases: A Black man accused of trying to enter a girl's room was captured and later found hanged, which the Shreveport accounts approve and the Milan Exchange calls a lynching (A1, A2, A3).

Spence was 'found hung' after his capture and was 'dealt with as he should have been', with no legal proceeding reported, and one paper says he was 'lynched' for an attempt at rape (A1, A2, A3); no account names his captors or says how many took part.

Both Louisiana texts are the same item, credited to the Shreveport Standard (A1) and the Shreveport Telegram (A2), and the Milan Exchange brief (A3) is a condensed state-news item, so all three appear to rest on one Shreveport account from 'a gentleman living in the neighborhood' (A1).

accounts.label: Shreveport newspaper account (neighborhood informant)
accounts.gist: A neighbor told the Shreveport paper that Spence had twice tried to enter an orphan girl's room at Spearman's, had once been tied and escaped, was captured on a third attempt, and was later found hanged; it approved the killing.

accounts.label: Louisiana news brief (Milan Exchange)
accounts.gist: Spence was lynched near Frog Levee, Caddo Parish, the previous week 'for an attempt at rape'.

framing.detail: Headed 'QUICK JUSTICE', the Shreveport Standard item calls the alleged act a 'damnable design' and says Spence 'was dealt with as he should have been'.
The Donaldsonville Chief reprinted the same approving text, credited to the Shreveport Telegram, among routine state news.
The Milan Exchange gave a one-line item that used the word 'lynched' and named the accusation as attempted rape, without comment.

conflicts.note: Likely a typesetting or OCR difference; the texts are otherwise the same.
The same text is credited to two Shreveport papers; one may have copied the other.
The two Louisiana texts agree on 'Frog Level'; 'Frog Levee' appears only in the condensed Tennessee brief.

record_check.dossier: Approximate only: before 1881-07-23 ('a few days ago' in a reprinted Shreveport item) and 'last week' per a 1881-07-30 brief; mid-July 1881 is supported, no exact day.
Attempting to enter the room of an orphan girl at Spearman's (three times); 'attempt at rape' per the Milan Exchange.
Not reported; captors and killers unnamed and their number not given.
Alleged attempted entry into a girl's room / 'attempt at rape'; Shreveport paper: 'dealt with as he should have been'.
Single source: all three reports trace to one Shreveport account from a neighborhood informant.
Initials given as 'J. E.' in one reprint and 'J. B.' in another.

info: Found hanged 'a few days' before the Shreveport report reprinted on 1881-07-23; 'last week' per a 1881-07-30 brief; exact date not given
